title: inference_in_lean, explained
h1: First-order logic and resolution in Lean 4: why every resolution step preserves truth
lead: Resolution, the inference rule behind many automated theorem provers, never derives a false clause from true ones. The project proves this soundness for ground (variable-free) resolution and factorisation, and for the general first-order versions that use a most general unifier. It also proves that a whole proof is sound once each of its single steps is. Those proofs are complete in the source. The only sorry is in the hard direction of the unification theorem (every unifiable problem has a most general unifier), and the soundness proofs don't use it.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of Norman Lohrer and Samuel Leßmann's Lean 4 formalisation of first-order logic (syntax, semantics, substitutions, unifiers) and of the soundness of ground and general resolution, following Chapter 3 of LMU's Automated Theorem Proving lecture notes.
startNote: Start with the headline, soundness of general resolution, and the two rules it covers: resolution and factorisation. To see what “sound” means, read Soundness, clause-set entailment and why sound steps give sound proofs. The building blocks are terms, clauses, substitutions and evaluation.
sizeNote: About 2,200 lines of Lean in 7 library files (plus about 330 lines of course exercises, not covered here). It targets Lean 4.34 (release candidate) with Mathlib.
agentCtx: A Lean 4 + Mathlib formalisation of first-order logic syntax and semantics, substitutions and unifiers, inference systems and proofs, and the soundness of ground and general (unifier-based) resolution and factorisation, following Chapter 3 of LMU's Automated Theorem Proving notes.

gloss.Set: Mathlib's Set α: a set of elements of type α, i.e. a predicate on α. Used here for sets of clauses and sets of free variables.
gloss.List: Lean's List α: a finite ordered list. Clauses are lists of literals, and function arguments are lists of terms.
